historical_significance: Richard Phillips Feynman (May 11, 1918 - February 15, 1988) was an American theoretical physicist, pioneer of quantum electrodynamics (QED). He revolutionized particle physics with Feynman diagrams, a visual notation for particle interactions, and developed the path integral formulation of quantum mechanics. He shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics with Julian Schwinger and Sin-Itiro Tomonaga for QED renormalization. He also joined the Manhattan Project, served on the Rogers Commission investigating the Challenger disaster (famously demonstrating the O-ring's failure with ice water), and popularized physics through The Feynman Lectures and the Feynman Technique of learning by teaching.
